Title: Efficacité de l’urétéroscopie souple versus lithotritie extracorporelle dans le traitement des calculs du rein
Author: Ravier et al.
Comment: For the synthesis contract, randomized denominators were retained (URSs 14; LEC 16) and unobserved outcomes were treated as unsuccessful. The paper does not print success counts. Counts were reconstructed from its conservative ITT ('biais maximum') percentages: the paired maximum-/minimum-bias percentages imply post-exclusion randomized-arm denominators of 9 for URSs (33.3%=3/9; 77.8%=7/9) and 13 for LEC (46.2%=6/13; 53.8%=7/13), yielding 3 and 6 observed successes, respectively; the 8 participants excluded before treatment remain in the randomized denominators as non-successes. This reconstruction should be sensitivity-tested because the arm-specific 9/13 denominators are implied rather than printed explicitly. Table 2 headers (URSs n=10; LEC n=12) reflect treatment received after one crossover and are not randomized-arm denominators. The Results prose is rendered as a 3-mm threshold, whereas Methods explicitly defines success as residual fragments <4 mm; the protocol/Methods definition was used.
Design Type: Prospective open-label parallel-group randomized controlled feasibility trial
Study Environment: Hospices Civils de Lyon hospitals, France
Medium: Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy versus flexible ureteroscopy with Holmium-YAG laser lithotripsy
Participant type: Adults with a single renal stone 5–20 mm requiring treatment
Recruitment source: Patients presenting between May 2012 and February 2014 at Hôpital Édouard-Herriot or Centre Hospitalier Lyon-Sud
Outcome measurement: Approximately 3-month imaging assessment; protocol specified noncontrast CT, although the Results state that some participants received ultrasound plus standard radiography. Success was no residual fragment or residual fragments <4 mm according to Methods.

effect_direction: RR > 1 favors ESWL; RR < 1 favors RIRS
